text:
I rise early at the day's first light,

after a light and measured sleep,

and sleep has only this heaviness:

not sleeping with your eyes, my Lesbia.


This obstinacy follows me inseparably,

my contemplation and your care,

in the house, on the mountain and in the meadow,

and in the warmest and the coldest season;


at table I contemplate your face,

night comes and I see you plainly;

for even though my loving soul reproaches me,


how can it believe that you are absent,

if there is no hour, minute, or instant

in which it does not see you very present?

translation.title: He Writes to Absent Lesbia...
translation.editorial_note: The translation keeps the absent beloved as continuously present in the speaker's perception.
